correctness.rationale: For fair binary input, successive 1-locations have independent geometric gaps; parity gives exact initial (2/3,1/3) and flip/stay (2/3,1/3). Published Theorems 2.4, 3.4 supply Lebesgue-invariance and strong mixing for F squared. Hence F_*nu=lambda, mu invariant; F squared ergodic proves F-ergodicity of mu; Birkhoff for continuous test functions and their F-compositions proves full-Lebesgue physical basin and phase-resolved limits. Stationary Markov flip ergodic theorem gives exponent log3-(2/3)log2 on nu-generic points, iid flip theorem exponent log3-(1/2)log2 on lambda-generic points. Comparing with lambda 2^{-n} and proving terminal binary runs O(log n) by Borel–Cantelli transfers dyadic exponents to Euclidean ball local dimensions. All quantified almost-sure domains and no independent mathematical audit are distinguished. checker replayed 2090 finite tests; finite tests not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: A published 2021 open question asks for non-atomic invariant measures of this erasing map. The explicit probability is invariant, ergodic and physical for a full-Lebesgue basin, despite having mutually singular positive-mass components. Its local dimension is nonconstant on an ergodic probability, an informative and unusual boundary phenomenon for this densely discontinuous system. Exact component masses and sharp values are natural statistical and geometric invariants, not arbitrary finite computations. The theorem is a compact synthesis, not a classification of all invariant measures.
